thesis: A 200 person family trades company put a machine on its after hours phone, kept its own people on the day shift, and stopped paying anybody to sit up all night waiting for a call.

vocabulary_lock.the_bottleneck: the after hours phone (never 'customer experience', never 'the call center problem', never 'communications')
vocabulary_lock.the_thing_bought: a voice platform (Avoca). Never 'an AI agent', never 'a bot'.
vocabulary_lock.the_people: CSRs on the day shift. Never 'agents', which would collide with the ladder vocabulary.
vocabulary_lock.the_rung: rung 4, a workflow. Named in plain words on slide 4 and again on slide 5.
vocabulary_lock.units: dollars per month everywhere. Seconds for the threshold. Days for the ramp. Never mix in hours.

slides.promise: makes the reader want to know what an ordinary trades company was paying to answer a phone at night, and what they did about it
makes the reader think that is basically us, and plants that this shop ran its own phones around the clock
makes the cost concrete and asks what you could possibly put on those hours instead
shows the mechanism and the seven second line, and opens the question of whether the machine would do better alone
answers that question with the seller's own number and makes the reader want to know what the arrangement actually bought Wilson
gives the keepable bounded number and opens what signing up for this would take
gives the plan and its honest holes, and opens whether any of it survives the trip north
lands it in Anchorage, names where it does not work, and leaves one thing to do Monday
seals the thesis as a shape and makes the single ask

honesty_spine: Every number on every slide carries its label in the same breath. The dominant label is that these are the owner's own figures, said on a podcast he co-hosts, in episodes his vendor sponsors. There is no independent corroboration and the deck never implies there is. The cost after-figure is drawn and written as a BOUND, never as a point value.
